html:
A war that began in January 2012 when Tuareg rebels and jihadist groups attacked in northern Mali, and soon after soldiers overthrew the government in Bamako.

The rebels took the north and declared a state of Azawad; then jihadists linked to al-Qaeda pushed them aside, imposed harsh law and destroyed saints' tombs in Timbuktu, a crime later tried at the International Criminal Court. French troops drove them from the towns in 2013, and a UN force stayed for ten years. The war spread to central Mali and to Burkina Faso and Niger. After coups in 2020 and 2021, the junta expelled French and UN forces and turned to Russia. See also the Tuareg.
sum: A war that began in January 2012 when Tuareg rebels and jihadist groups attacked in northern Mali, and soon after soldiers overthrew the government in Bamako.
